title: game
description: A game is a voluntary activity conducted within agreed-upon boundaries — rules, a playing space, a duration — where participants make choices that affect outcomes. Four features recur: rules, objectives, uncertainty, voluntariness. Not itself play — a game is play plus agreed structure (see ../../../../../schemas/glossary/terms/play.schema.json).

rules.description: The constraints on legal action; rules make choice meaningful — without constraint there is free play, not a game.

objectives.description: What participants orient toward; need not be competitive (a collaborative story counts), but participants can distinguish moves that advance it from moves that don't.

uncertainty.description: The sources that make choices matter; a known outcome makes the activity a performance, not a game.

voluntary.description: Entering the game is a choice held under the lusory attitude; compelled participation retains the mechanics while losing the character of a game.

players.description: The participants whose choices affect the outcome.

state.description: The complete description of the game at a moment.
